source: (cd lp-fw/fw-esp32c6 && cargo build --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --profile release-esp32 --features esp32c6,test_shader_compile_incremental) && cargo run -q -p lp-emu-esp32c6 --release -- --elf target/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/release-esp32/fw-esp32c6 --time-grade t2 --usb-sj file:target/validate/shader-compile-stress.cap --usb-sj-tried file:target/validate/shader-compile-stress.tried --usb-host attached --timeout 120s --wall-timeout 2400 --strict-bus --exit-on '[inc-shader-compile] === DONE ===' --efuse-mac a0:f2:62:87:b4:8c --efuse-rev 0.2
note: --link override: this run's link is `usb-serial-jtag`, not payload `shader-compile-stress`'s own `uart0-spike` (`validate.toml`/`payload.rs` are unchanged — this is a per-run choice, recorded here and in `firmware_features` so a reader of the transcript alone can tell it from a run of the payload's default link).

trust.because: the same allocator and the same RAM model as t1, and the harness's 372 memory values are identical under both grades — a time grade must not move a heap byte. The one figure that does move is the idle stack high-water mark (11,432 B under t1, 11,752 B under t2), which is interleaving, not memory: the deepest interrupted call chain is not the same chain
t2 uses the per-class cycle model rather than one cycle per instruction, and no transcript grades it either. It is a rung up the ladder, not a promise about milliseconds on silicon
direct load prints no ROM or bootloader banner; the time grade changes nothing about that. M7 owns it

the same host model as t1, and the same four transcripts stand behind it — `boot-idle` is recorded on this grade too and its heap figures are t1's to the byte, which is what a time grade must never move. `modeled` for t1's reason: the evidence is here to be weighed, and the silicon half of the negative control is owed

the same pin observation as t1, on the same two committed captures: the rmt-chase checksums agree on all 768 frames and the shipped image's first lit frame off gpio18 is the host oracle's (`shader-oracle-walk`, crc 0x55772254), with only the frame COUNT by the sentinel moving between the grades (39 against t1's 59 in three seconds — the clock's, reported as timing). The same reason for the grade: the fabric and the decoder are in the machine, not on a scope, and no silicon pin transcript exists
the same UART0 model as t1: the bytes are the guest's, a live socket's arrival times are the host's
